title: Terpene mechanism, evidence and safety records

policy.medicalClaimPolicy: This dataset describes research findings and uncertainty. It does not diagnose, treat, recommend a dose, or establish a therapeutic effect in humans.
policy.rule: A receptor interaction or animal outcome must not be displayed as a proven human therapeutic effect.
policy.entourageRule: Do not present cannabinoid-terpene synergy as established clinical fact unless supported by compound-specific human evidence.

compoundEvidence.finding: (E)-β-caryophyllene has demonstrated selective CB2 receptor binding and functional agonism in receptor/cellular experiments; animal studies also support CB2-dependent biological effects.
compoundEvidence.humanEvidenceStatus: mechanism not established as a therapeutic effect in humans
compoundEvidence.limitations: Receptor activity and animal outcomes do not establish efficacy, dose, safety, or treatment benefit in people.

compoundEvidence.finding: Reviews report preclinical interactions with α2-adrenergic and TRPV1 targets among proposed mechanisms for β-myrcene.
compoundEvidence.limitations: Target-level or animal findings should not be translated into a predictable human effect from a Cannabis sample.

compoundEvidence.finding: Preclinical literature summarized in reviews reports borneol activation of TRPM8 under experimental conditions.
compoundEvidence.limitations: Experimental receptor activation does not establish a therapeutic effect, effective dose, or expected outcome from plant material.

generalEvidence.title: Entourage-effect claims
generalEvidence.finding: Cannabis terpenes and cannabinoids may share or influence biological targets, but proposed synergy is compound-, model-, dose- and endpoint-dependent. Current literature does not justify treating a generic terpene profile as proof of a predictable clinical entourage effect.
generalEvidence.limitations: Do not infer therapeutic synergy from co-occurrence alone.

safety.concern: Oxidized linalool can contribute to allergic contact dermatitis in susceptible individuals.
safety.evidenceContext: dermal/cosmetic exposure literature summarized in review
safety.limitation: Risk depends on exposure route, oxidation state, concentration and individual susceptibility.

safety.concern: In vitro literature reports CYP3A4 inhibition by limonene or related preparations, creating a plausible interaction question for drugs metabolized through that pathway.
safety.limitation: In vitro enzyme inhibition does not establish the magnitude or clinical significance of an interaction at typical Cannabis exposure levels.

safety.concern: High-dose or concentrated isolated-terpene exposure is not equivalent to smelling or handling intact plant material; dose and route can change toxicology substantially.
safety.evidenceContext: animal and toxicology literature summarized in review
safety.limitation: Do not use preclinical high-dose findings to infer toxicity or safety at unrelated exposure levels.
